bull.b: Growing recurring cloud revenue and a rising share from production applications indicate that customers are moving beyond experimentation toward operational use. This strengthens revenue quality, supports repeat engagement, and could improve the scalability of D-Wave’s software and services model over the next several quarters.

The sharp increase in remaining performance obligations provides meaningful contracted visibility relative to the company’s current revenue base. Recognition over the next two years can support commercial scaling, validate customer commitment, and reduce reliance on entirely new bookings for near-term growth.

Milestone-based government funding can help finance advanced hardware research, domestic capability expansion, and commercialization without relying solely on operating cash flow. The program also reinforces institutional support for D-Wave’s technology and may accelerate its dual-platform development roadmap.

bear.b: D-Wave’s strong gross margins have not translated into operating profitability because its cost base remains very large relative to revenue. Continued losses limit internally funded investment, increase dependence on external capital, and make execution toward sustainable earnings a central business risk.

Persistent operating and free-cash-flow deficits mean the company continues to consume capital while commercial revenue is still developing. Although liquidity is substantial, prolonged burn can reduce financial flexibility, constrain investment choices, and increase reliance on future financing or funding programs.

Revenue remains vulnerable to the timing of large annealing system deliveries, creating uneven results and limited visibility between contract signing and installation. Dependence on two expected 2026 shipments makes near-term growth sensitive to execution, customer acceptance, and deployment schedules.
